newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end with mild gain.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end with mild gain.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended a featureless session modestly higher, waiting for the parade of second-quarter earnings reports to begin.
A large number of U.S. companies will release quarterly earnings results this week, and some market participants were leery of the potential for a surprise disappointment from a bellwether company.
Overall, traders and analysts said they expected earnings to be in line with expectations or possibly exceed forecasts.
Among the big companies releasing earnings Tuesday are Intel Corp.
S&P floor traders said the market also suffered this session from a dose of the summer doldrums.
"I don't think any big numbers are going to shake us out of this funk," said one trader.
September S&Ps traded up to a high of 929.70 in the morning, slipped below unchanged around midday, then bounced back late in the session to end slightly higher on the day.
"We overshot on the downside on no volume and rallied back on low volume," the trader said.
A lack of market-moving U.S. economic data helped limit the activity in stock index futures, traders said.
The market brushed off June manufacturing data from the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta. The Atlanta Fed reported its industry business activity index rose to 17.5 from a revised 17.3 in May.
June U.S. retail sales data will be released on Tuesday and are projected to rise 0.2 percent.
September S&Ps remained below the most recent contract high of 932.25 set one week ago.

S&P 500 futures ended up 2.45 points at 926.85, Nasdaq 100s rose 27.65 to 1054.25, Russell 2000s were up 1.35 points at 408.45, Nikkei 225 index futures rose 405.0 to 20,325.0 and Midcap 400s rose 1.05 points to 303.50.
